newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma urges halt to UES sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma urges halt to UES sale.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament on Sunday called on President Boris Yeltsin and the government to halt the sale of 8.5 percent of national power company Unified Energy System.
Deputies voted by 277 to one to back an appeal to scrap the cash auction, due to be completed by December 23.

They said in the appeal that the money to be made from the sale would not compensate for the loss of control over the strategically important power generation industry and that more of the company could fall into foreign hands.
The Federal Securities Corporation said last month that 3.66 billion shares in UES would be sold at a minimum 500 roubles (about $0.09) each.

"(UES) belongs to the strategic elements of Russian industry and the $350-400 million which might be received by the federal budget from the sale of shares in UES will not replace those losses linked to the inability of the state to control the power generation complex," the appeal said.
UES shares stood on Sunday, a working day in Russia, at $0.0825 each. But the Duma appeal said their real value was about 8-10 times this sum.

It said foreigners held 22.5 percent of UES shares but that after the auction this could rise to 30-31 percent, giving them influence over many company decisions. The state currently has a 60 percent stake in the company.
UES asset management director Alexander Lopatin welcomed the fact the Duma had taken up the question of the auction.
"We are not against it, let anyone buy it. We are simply drawing the attention of the main shareholder (the state) to the consequences," he told Reuters.
